article_title: Automated Gaze-Based Identification of Students’ Strategies in Histogram Tasks through an Interpretable Mathematical Model and a Machine Learning Algorithm
citation: Boels, L., Garcia Moreno-Esteva, E., Bakker, A., & Drijvers, P. (2024). Automated Gaze-Based Identification of Students' Strategies in Histogram Tasks through an Interpretable Mathematical Model and a Machine Learning Algorithm. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 34, 931-973. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-023-00368-9
title: Attentional anchors as perceptual forms of gaze patterns that facilitate task-specific strategies
description: The article draws on enactivism and embodied cognition to interpret students' gaze patterns as attentional anchors (AAs). An AA is "a real or imagined object, area, or other behavior of the perceptual manifold that emerges to facilitate motor-action coordination." In this study, stable horizontal or vertical scanpaths on the graph area are interpreted as AAs that facilitate students' imagined actions for finding the mean from a histogram, regardless of strategy correctness. The AA concept is used both to ground the theoretical interpretation of gaze patterns and to guide the construction of the IMM.
requirements: The AA concept requires that gaze patterns form a stable scanpath with multiple aligned fixations and saccades that students themselves recognize as relevant to their strategy
constraints: The relationship between eye movements and cognitive processes is not straightforward, and not every eye movement is part of a student's strategy
target_learning_goals: Estimating the arithmetic mean from histogram representations
Correct interpretation of histograms versus case-value plots
examples: Student L10 described chopping and flattening bars (compensation) while gaze data showed a stable horizontal scanpath interpreted as an AA for an incorrect case-value plot strategy

citation: D’Mello, S. K. (2016). Giving Eyesight to the Blind: Towards Attention-Aware AIED. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-016-0104-1
title: Three-component attentional computing architecture for attention-aware learning environments
description: The article defines an attention-aware learning environment as one that can "detects and (re)directs the learner’s attention in near real-time in order to achieve some desired outcome". It sketches a three-component attentional computing layer: (1) a mechanism to monitor where attention appears to be directed (eye tracking), (2) a mechanism to diagnose the underlying attentional state, and (3) strategies to (re)direct attention as needed.
requirements: Requires eye tracking to monitor where attention appears to be directed, computational techniques for real-time attentional state diagnosis, and interventions to (re)direct attentional focus.
target_learners: learners using intelligent tutoring systems and learning environments
target_learning_goals: maintaining optimal attentional states during learning

Assistive technology for the inclusion of students with disabilities: a systematic review. Educational technology research and development, 70, 1911–1930. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-022-10127-7
title: Three thematic clusters organise assistive technology research: enabler of inclusion, barriers to effective use, and possibilities and benefits
description: The review's keyword co-occurrence analysis (VOSviewer) of 45 Key Words Plus from the 31 studies identifies three thematic clusters structuring the field: "AT as an enabler of inclusion and participation" (cluster 1), "barriers to effective use of AT" (cluster 2) and "possibilities and benefits of AT" (cluster 3). Cluster 1 includes terms such as assistive technology, inclusion, software, web, tablet and robotic; cluster 2 highlights teacher training, education, higher education and school; cluster 3 highlights autonomy, participation, social skill, access and motivation. A bibliometric density map places student, disability, assistive technology and teacher in the central yellow zone of highest co-occurrence.
requirements: Keyword co-occurrence analysis using VOSviewer on the automatically extracted keywords of the reviewed studies
constraints: Derived from the 31 studies included in this review, limited to four databases and 2009–2020
target_learners: students with disabilities across primary, secondary and university education
target_learning_goals: inclusion and accessibility of the curriculum for students with disabilities
examples: The labelled bibliometric map (Fig. 9) shows the three clusters generated by keyword similarity, with node size and distance setting the relationship between terms

citation: José María Fernández-Batanero, Marta Montenegro-Rueda, José Fernández-Cerero, Inmaculada García-Martínez. (2022). title: Systematic review corpus of 31 empirical studies on assistive technology for students with disabilities (2009–2020)
description: A PRISMA-guided corpus of 31 peer-reviewed empirical studies (2009–2020) on AT for inclusion of students with disabilities, identified from Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC and PsycINFO plus manual reference-list searching. From 216 initially selected articles, duplicates and ineligible items were removed through double screening using inclusion–exclusion criteria (publication date, type, focus, method), yielding the final 31. constraints: Selection restricted to the four databases chosen by the authors, which the authors state as a limitation of the paper

article_title: “We are too dumb for this”: a critical discourse analysis of stereotypical attributions to struggle with computational thinking
citation: Lucas Vasconcelos. (2025). “We are too dumb for this”: a critical discourse analysis of stereotypical attributions to struggle with computational thinking. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10532-8
title: Attribution theory's three dimensions (locus, stability, controllability) as a framework for analyzing struggle discourse in computational thinking
description: Attribution theory describes how individuals interpret and explain the causes of events and behaviors. The article uses its three dimensions — locus (dispositional vs. situational), stability (permanent vs. temporary), and controllability — as the coding framework for preservice teachers' attributions during struggle with computational thinking. The article states that "Attributions can differ in three fundamental aspects: locus (origin), stability, and controllability", and that attributions influence motivation, emotional responses, and subsequent behavior, making them a lens for identifying stereotypical versus non-stereotypical explanations of struggle.
requirements: Analysis requires discourse data captured as attributions occur, which the article argues minimizes self-report biases such as memory lapses.
constraints: The article frames its critical discourse analysis through a Western lens on computer science stereotypes, noting stereotypes differ in Eastern countries.
target_learners: K-12 learners in computer science education
target_learning_goals: understanding causal attributions during productive struggle
promoting growth-oriented attributions
examples: The study coded 27 discourse episodes in NVivo by locus, stability, and controllability, classifying statements like "Neither of us know computers" as dispositional, uncontrollable, and permanent.

citation: Trevisan, Ottavia; Marcato, Filippo; Christensen, Rhonda. (2026). Pixels and Pedagogy: MISTT's Insights into Evolving Teacher Identities When Technology Comes to Play. COMPUTERS & EDUCATION. https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2026.105601

citation: Charles Munter, Paul Cobb, and Calli Shekell. (2014). The Use of Program Theory in Mathematics Education Evaluation Research. SREE Spring 2014 Conference Abstract. https://www.sree.org
title: Program evaluation of mathematics interventions should attend to and use program theory alongside methodological rigor, because WWC specifications alone are inadequate
description: The article argues that evaluation research of mathematics programs needs to improve its attention to and use of program theory: articulating a testable causal chain, asking questions about mechanisms, employing varied outcome measures aligned with program intent, and assessing both process and structure implementation fidelity. Its analysis indicates that "WWC’s methodological specifications are inadequate because they overlook understanding and using theory in evaluation design and implementation." Both method and theory are held necessary for valid evidence on which policy and curriculum adoption decisions can be based.
requirements: Evaluators articulate the theory underlying the program in each step of evaluation, from design to interpretation of findings
constraints: The review found that despite more than 25 years of calls, the field has seen little change in attending to program theory
target_learning_goals: Valid evidence on the effectiveness of mathematics programs to guide policy and curriculum adoption decisions
examples: The review coded 36 WWC-qualified reports and found evaluators rarely articulated a testable causal chain for how a program was theorized to achieve its goals
key_sources: Charles Munter, Paul Cobb, and Calli Shekell. (2014). The Use of Program Theory in Mathematics Education Evaluation Research. SREE Spring 2014 Conference Abstract. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED563007

article_title: Examining Personalisation of Instruction, Attitudes toward and Achievement in Mathematics Word Problems among Nigerian Senior Secondary School Students
citation: Awofala, A. O. A. (2014). Examining Personalisation of Instruction, Attitudes toward and Achievement in Mathematics Word Problems among Nigerian Senior Secondary School Students. International Journal of Education in Mathematics, Science and Technology, 2(4), 273-288. https://www.ijemst.com
title: ATMWPI, SII and IPMW instruments used to measure attitudes, elicit preferences and deliver personalised versus non-personalised instruction

"The personalised version provided familiar, relevant problem contexts and was written by incorporating the most popular referents (places, foods, sports, etc.) from the SII", while the non-personalised version used standard textbook problems with minimal contextual information; both incorporated Polya's four-part strategy.

constraints: The personalised and non-personalised versions required the same computational skills and used identical numbers, differing only in problem context
target_learners: senior secondary school year one students
target_learning_goals: attitudes toward mathematics word problems
achievement in mathematics word problems
examples: 78% of participants wrote in Tantalizer as their favourite fast food mall, which was then used to formulate a personalised word problem about the cost of meat pies

article_title: Emergent Literacy Development and Computer Assisted Instruction
citation: Trotti, J., Hendricks, R., & Bledsoe, C. (2017). Emergent Literacy Development and Computer Assisted Instruction. SRATE Journal, 26(1), 30-39. https://www.sratejournal.org
title: Attribution theory and sociocultural theory as a framework for explaining pre-K students' poor performance with independent CAI
description: The article interprets its findings through two frameworks. Because children worked independently during CAI, "social interactions with other children and the teacher were limited," which the authors use to explain the control group's advantage.
requirements: Individualized CAI within the classroom setting with auditory and visual reinforcement feedback, as both programs provided
constraints: The framework is applied to pre-K children working independently of one another during CAI; the article notes this limits social interaction
target_learners: at-risk four-year-old prekindergarten students eligible for free or reduced lunch
target_learning_goals: emergent literacy skills including phonemic awareness, phonics, letter recognition, and vocabulary
examples: Students cried or ignored the teacher when asked to use either computer program, which the authors attribute to beliefs of incapability per attribution theory

description: The article frames orphans' insecure attachment and weak social skills through Bowlby's attachment theory: "according to the attachment theory, there is a relationship between the human mental health and his or her relationship with the attachment pictures". constraints: Applied in the article to orphans deprived of early maternal emotional bonds

examples: The article cites Bowlby (1980), Freud (1933) and Klein (1950) as theoretical foundations for the intervention

citation: Doxey, J., Baty, B. J., Bisordi, K., & Dixon, S. (2026). Assessing genetic counselors' teaching experience and approaches to teaching in the classroom. Journal of Genetic Counseling. https://doi.org/10.1002/jgc4.70207
title: Approaches to Teaching Inventory—Revised (ATI-R) two-scale framework for describing teaching approaches
description: The ATI-R is a 22-item inventory with two 11-item scales measuring approaches to teaching: the Information Transfer/Teacher-focused (ITTF) scale and the Conceptual Change/Student-focused (CCSF) scale, each scored as the mean of 5-point item responses. The ITTF approach focuses on "transmitting information to their students based on their own knowledge" with little interaction, while the CCSF approach aims to change students' conceptions and encourages students to construct their own knowledge. This study used the ATI-R to assess genetic counselors' classroom teaching approaches and to test whether approaches relate to teaching experience and student populations taught.
requirements: Respondents complete the 22 items on a 5-point scale rating how true each statement is of their own teaching; scores reflect self-perceptions of teaching approach.
constraints: The article notes the ATI-R measures participants' self-perceptions of their approaches to teaching, which may not reflect their true approaches to teaching in practice.
target_learners: Genetic counselors teaching in classroom settings
target_learning_goals: Describing and measuring teachers' approaches to teaching (teacher-focused versus student-focused)
Understanding how teaching approaches relate to teaching experience
examples: In this study, 89 genetic counselors completed the ATI-R; the mean CCSF score was 3.6 (SD = 0.7) and the mean ITTF score was 3.3 (SD = 0.7).

article_title: The Academic Threat Appraisal Ratio Scale (ATARS): Insights into attainment, academic progression, and retention in higher education.
citation: Cassidy, S. (2026). The Academic Threat Appraisal Ratio Scale (ATARS): Insights into attainment, academic progression, and retention in higher education. British Journal of Educational Psychology, 96, 90–107. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjep.12780
title: Academic Threat Appraisal Ratio Scale (ATARS)
description: The ATARS is a two-item self-report measure adapted from Tomaka et al.'s (1993) cognitive appraisal ratio and Vine et al. (2015) for use at the start of a degree course. It asks how demanding the course will be (Item A) and how able the student is to cope (Item B), each on a 1–6 scale; subtracting A from B yields a Demand Resource Evaluation Score (DRES) ranging −5 to 5, where positive scores are interpreted as a challenge state and negative scores as a threat state. The article presents it as a "relatively simple, valid, and scalable" tool for early screening enabling targeted student support.
requirements: Completed prospectively, in anticipation of completing the degree course, i.e., before the motivated performance situation unfolds
constraints: The author calls for further validation: content-expert review with students to check item understanding across groups including cultural variations, comparisons with physiological and multi-item measures, and test–retest studies to determine optimal completion timing
target_learning_goals: early identification of students at risk of poor attainment and non-progression
examples: In the study, students completed the ATARS on paper during scheduled lectures at the start of the degree; the appendix suggests adaptations such as adding 'this year' or substituting 'degree course' for 'exam', dissertation, presentation, etc.

title: ATI TEAS admission assessment and RN Content Mastery Series Fundamentals exam as predictor and outcome measures

title: Approaches to Teaching Inventory framework: teacher-focused (ITTF) versus student-focused (CCSF) approaches and five qualitatively different approaches

examples: The EM/EA video and poster instructions were designed as the framing manipulation predicted by this framework to shift learners' motivational mind sets

title: Attention boost effect as a proposed mechanism for observer-tool learning in simulation
description: The article invokes the attention boost effect to explain how completing an observer tool might enhance vicarious learning during simulation. The authors state that the theory "suggests that when two actions are performed simultaneously (in the present study, observing the other student and filling out the OT), attention is increased", and that this would be even more true when the elements to observe are frequent. They connect this to social learning theory, in which vicarious learning occurs because observing others shows how behaviours are produced and reproduced.

constraints: The article presents this mechanism as an explanation, not a tested result of this trial; the global-performance result was null
target_learners: medical students acting as observers in simulation sessions
target_learning_goals: improved acquisition of procedural and knowledge outcomes from observation of peers
examples: The authors propose the attention boost effect to explain why OT use might reinforce attention during training, while noting the wider literature on observer tools is limited, heterogeneous and controversial

citation: Van Hootegem, A., Røgeberg, O., Bratsberg, B., & Lyngstad, T. H. (2023). Correlation between cognitive ability and educational attainment weakens over birth cohorts. Scientific Reports, 13, 17747. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-44605-6
title: Decoupling account: educational attainment is becoming a weaker signal of cognitive ability, against the meritocratic-alignment hypothesis
description: The article frames its findings against the hypothesis that broadened educational opportunity makes attainment an increasingly meritocratic indicator of ability, and reports data that "goes counter to the hypothesis that educational attainment increasingly aligns with individual level ability as educational opportunities are broadened." The authors propose candidate mechanisms: education may have become less selective, new vocational tracks may emphasize practical skills, and, drawing on signaling theory, credentials may have become noisier signals as the cost of completion fell. The correlation remains moderate to strong, so ability stays coupled to attainment.
requirements: Population-wide cognitive ability measures and educational registers linked across birth cohorts to estimate cohort-specific correlations
constraints: Findings are for Norwegian men only; no cognitive scores were available for women
The conscription test has remained essentially unchanged since the early 1950s and items may function differently due to changed social context
The finding does not show why the correlation declined; competing explanations are offered, not tested
target_learning_goals: Understanding how educational attainment relates to cognitive ability as educational systems expand
examples: Norway expanded compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years in 1969, granted universal rights to higher secondary education in 1994, and lowered school starting age to 6 in 1997
Vocationally oriented tertiary institutions in Norway offer wide program ranges with lower rejection rates and students with lower average grades
